capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

- For the first statement, take \(x\in f^{-1}(s)\). Since \(s\subseteq f(t)\), write \(f(x)=f(y)\) for some \(y\in t\). Then \(f(y)\in s\), so both \(x\) and \(y\) lie in \(f^{-1}(s)\). Injectivity of \(f\) on this preimage gives \(x=y\), hence \(x\in t\). The essential mechanism is transporting membership through the image witness and then applying restricted injectivity.

- For the second statement, prove set equality by extensionality and case analysis on \(x:\alpha\oplus\beta\). If \(x=\operatorname{inl}(a)\), it is visibly in the range and `isLeft` is true. If \(x=\operatorname{inr}(b)\), it cannot belong to the range of `inl`, and `isLeft` evaluates to false.

The useful intermediate goals are therefore the two set inclusions/membership equivalences, with `Sum` case analysis handling the second one.
